title: Boss: build a tiny Git
summary: Hash a working tree into blobs and a tree, write a commit chain, and detect tampering, all with Git's real formats.

steps.title: The scene
steps.body: A teammate claims *"Git is magic."* You will show them it is four object formats and SHA-1. Using only what you built in this module, you will turn a folder into a real Git tree id, chain real commits, and catch a tampered object, matching what `git` itself prints.

steps.title: Snapshot a flat folder
prompt: Write `SnapshotTree(Dictionary<string, string> files)` for a folder with **no sub-directories**: hash every file as a blob (mode `100644`), then return the tree id. Include `BlobId` and `TreeId`.
The check uses a folder with just `hello.txt` = `"hello\n"`, whose real tree id is `aaa96ced2d9a1c8e72c56b253a0e2fe78393feb7`.
solution: static string TreeId(List<(string Mode, string Name, string Id)> entries)
string Key((string Mode, string Name, string Id) e) => e.Mode == "40000" ? e.Name + "/" : e.Name;
hints: Map each file to `("100644", name, BlobId(content))`.
template: Dojo.Check("content matters", SnapshotTree(new() { ["hello.txt"] = "hello!\n" }) != "aaa96ced2d9a1c8e72c56b253a0e2fe78393feb7", "a different file must give a different tree");
Dojo.Check("names matter", SnapshotTree(new() { ["hi.txt"] = "hello\n" }) != "aaa96ced2d9a1c8e72c56b253a0e2fe78393feb7", "renaming must change the tree");

steps.title: Snapshot with folders
prompt: Now support paths with `/`. Write `SnapshotTreeDeep(Dictionary<string, string> files)`:
- Files directly in this folder become blob entries (`100644`).
- For each first path segment that is a folder, recursively snapshot the files under it (with that prefix removed) and add a `40000` entry for the sub-tree.
Include `BlobId` and `TreeId`. The real repo with `hello.txt` and `src/App.cs` = `"class App {}\n"` has root tree `a45ecc342b99792adf11582f987b95ee5fcd810e`.
solution: static string TreeId(List<(string Mode, string Name, string Id)> entries)
string Key((string Mode, string Name, string Id) e) => e.Mode == "40000" ? e.Name + "/" : e.Name;
var entries = new List<(string Mode, string Name, string Id)>();
foreach (var group in files.Where(f => f.Key.Contains('/')).GroupBy(f => f.Key.Split('/')[0]))
var sub = group.ToDictionary(f => f.Key[(group.Key.Length + 1)..], f => f.Value);
hints: For each group build a new dictionary with the prefix removed: `key[(folder.Length + 1)..]`.
Call yourself on it and add `("40000", folder, id)`.

steps.title: Chain commits
prompt: Write `Chain(List<string> messages, string tree, string person, long time)` that creates one commit per message, all with the same tree, each one's parent being the previous commit (the first has none). Return the list of commit ids in creation order. Include `CommitText`/`CommitId`.

With the hello tree, `Ada <ada@example.com>` and time `1700000000`, messages `Add hello`, `Second` give the real ids `b0313dbfea675ba0583498b791d496a6786d5f5f` and `1b0ca98a4adf40e6313895d1b0500672ee30d710`.
starter: static List<string> Chain(List<string> messages, string tree, string person, long time)
solution: static string CommitText(string tree, List<string> parents, string person, long time, string message)
static string CommitId(string tree, List<string> parents, string person, long time, string message)
var body = Encoding.UTF8.GetBytes(CommitText(tree, parents, person, time, message));
static List<string> Chain(List<string> messages, string tree, string person, long time)
var parents = ids.Count == 0 ? new List<string>() : new List<string> { ids[^1] };
hints: Keep the ids in a list; the parent of each new commit is `ids[^1]`.
The first commit gets an empty parent list.
template: Dojo.Eq("matches git commit-tree", new List<string> { "b0313dbfea675ba0583498b791d496a6786d5f5f", "1b0ca98a4adf40e6313895d1b0500672ee30d710" }, Chain(new() { "Add hello", "Second" }, "aaa96ced2d9a1c8e72c56b253a0e2fe78393feb7", "Ada <ada@example.com>", 1700000000));
Dojo.Check("rewriting the first commit changes every later id", dojoA[1] != dojoB[1] && dojoA[2] != dojoB[2], "ids after a rewrite must all differ");

steps.title: Detect tampering
steps.prompt: `git fsck` verifies that every object's content still hashes to its name. Write `Corrupt(Dictionary<string, (string Type, string Content)> store)` returning the ids (sorted ordinal) whose stored content does **not** hash to the id. The hash is SHA-1 of `"<type> <byte length>\0" + content` (types here are `blob` and `commit`, stored as text).
starter: static List<string> Corrupt(Dictionary<string, (string Type, string Content)> store)
solution: static string ObjectId(string type, string content)
static List<string> Corrupt(Dictionary<string, (string Type, string Content)> store)
hints: Compare the recomputed id with the key.

Dojo.Eq("two tampered objects", new List<string> { "32f95c0d1244a78b2be1bab8de17906fabb2c4a8", "e69de29bb2d1d6434b8b29ae775ad8c2e48c5391" }, Corrupt(dojoStore));
